messages.subject: dartR version 2.0.4
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

This is just to let you know that the latest version of dartR (v 2.0.4) is now on CRAN and can be installed by typing in the R console:

> install.packages("dartR")

Below are described the improvements and bug fixes in this version.

Cheers,

Luis

Improvements:

- gl.plot.structure: CLUMPP and Clumpak approaches can be run without installing these programs. Improved plot and added options to customise it.

- gl.run.structure: Installation of StrataG is not necessary to run the function.

- gl.filter.allna: Add an option to recalculate loc.metrics.

- gl.filter.hwe and gl.report.hwe: Add the option to remove loci only if they are concurrently significant in more than N populations.

- gl.filter.maf: Add option to filter on minor allele frequency (MAC)

- gl.report.diversity: add the option to print or not the plot.

- gl2genepop: Add the option to choose from a 2 digits format or a 3 digits format as output. Populations can now be ordered using a vector.

- gl.dist.pop and gl.dist.ind: Add labels to the distance matrix.

- gl.diagnostics.hwe: Add option to compute or not standard errors.

- gl.read.dart: add the option to remove loci with all missing data.

- gl2vcf: Add alleles to @loc.all. The order of reference and alternative alleles is the same as the genlight object.

- various functions: Add a flag to check whether loci with all missing data have been filtered.

Bugs fixes:

- gl.filter.allna: Fix bug when more loci were filtered out with the option by.pop.

- gl.install.vanilla.dartR: Fix the bug that prevented installing the "dev" version.

- gl.report.sexlinked and gl.filter.sexlinked: Display now the same information.

- gl2plink: Fix bug in the name of chromosomes.

Many thanks for your help!

Best regards,
Chrys

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

The function actually copies the popgen file to the tempfile. The reason for this is that the Ne2-1L program is a bit of a beast to make sure all path are set correctly and much easier to run from within tempdir, where all path are known.

In case you want to run it per Hand, though maybe you can somehow increase the available space as the programm also creates some output files. [there is a free rcloud account where you can run R on linux and it should have enough space for a run (free for 20 hours a month or so)

Short description how to run per “hand”:

Yes you can create the genepop file with gl2genpop. The only “difficulty is then that you need another file (the info file that runs with Ne21L and its settings to estimate LD NE). This info file is created on the fly by the function. So you can copy it from tempdir and then run it per command line with the genepop file. From within tempdir. That saves that the file is copied over).

The file is called ‘info’ no extension and I attached an example file. Here you need to set the path etc.

In the manual the Nestimator 2 you find some more info on info :’)

The whole command is then

./Ne2-1L -i info xyz.gen

There is a helpfile (pdf) that explains how to run from command line) and it has also fully commented examples of the info file.

Hope that helps,

Regards, Bernd

Sorry to be back already! I do not know if my question is more related to dartR or to another software (namely NeEstimator2).

I tried to run an R script including the command dartR::gl.LDne(...) on a Linux server. Unfortunately, it apparently led to interferences with other jobs from the same cluster, because the binary Ne2-1L had opened temporary files on a disk with very limited space, leading to "saturation".

Is that something someone had experienced as well when using gl.LDNe on large genlight/genepop files (as of course, it requires a lot of pairwise comparisons to get measures of linkage disequilibrium)?

I was wondering if I could resolve the issue by modifying the function gl.LDNe() so the step gl2genepop() stores the genepop file in the working directory, instead of a temporary folder?

Many thanks for your help!

Best regards,

Chrys

Greetings,
I am a regular user of the dartR gl2fasta() command. Normally, when running this command with method parameter "method=1" I find a .fas file that is properly aligned and ready for downstream analysis. Today I found that the alignment (1,106 X ~300,000 bp) was not aligned properly, where some of the missing loci (encoded by a string of "N") were short by one bp. I have no problem fixing the issue, but I am curious if anyone else had the same issue, and if there is something I've done wrong and can avoid in the future.
Cheers,
Mike

Hi Gabriella,

In regards to gl.filter.secondaries, this function strips all but one SNP from each sequence tag, where the sequence tag happens to have been scored for more than one SNP. It, by default, selects one SNP at random, so you would expect slightly different results from one run to another.

With gl.report.secondaries, your question relates to the estimate of sequence tags that are invariant. The function does this by fitting a zero truncated Poisson distribution to the distribution of 'SNP frequencies per tag', then extrapolates to estimate the value for the zero class. This again, uses approximate techniques to achieve convergence to a solution, which has a small random element to it.  So you would expect slightly different results from one run to another.

gl.filter.sexlinked has undergone some serious re-coding between the two versions, which could explain why it is slightly more efficient in the latest version. Luis might be able to assist here.

Ditto gl.outflank.

You might also check if you have exactly the same filtering prior to the application of these functions in the two versions.

Hope this helps.

A
